method: Updates use verifiable rules, not neural network retraining. Up to 200 completed 10+0 games with confirmed identity are analyzed; very short games and special starting positions are excluded. A pattern requires errors across at least three games and three distinct positions. Only fully analyzed games count.

piece-loss.title: Losing pieces
piece-loss.observation: After these moves, the opponent’s principal reply captures a piece and the evaluation worsens.
piece-loss.goal: Find a move that keeps your pieces safe.
piece-loss.hint: Look at pieces that would be undefended after moving and the opponent’s captures.
piece-loss.rule: Before committing to a move, inspect the opponent's checks, captures, and threats against your most exposed piece.
piece-loss.contrast: If no reply wins material or forces a concession, continue with your plan.

missed-capture.title: Missed valuable captures
missed-capture.observation: The engine found a piece capture better than your move in these positions.
missed-capture.goal: Look for a useful capture and check the opponent’s reply.
missed-capture.hint: Look for attacked enemy pieces. Before capturing, calculate the recapture.
missed-capture.rule: Before choosing a plan, inspect every capture and calculate first those that change material or force a reply.
missed-capture.contrast: An available capture is not automatically good: check the recapture and the resulting position.

missed-mate.title: Missed mating opportunities
missed-mate.observation: The engine found a forced mate, but your move did not preserve a verified mate.
missed-mate.goal: Look for a forcing continuation against the king.
missed-mate.hint: Look at checks and the king’s escape squares; calculate all legal replies.
missed-mate.rule: When the opposing king is exposed, calculate every check before evaluating quiet moves.
missed-mate.contrast: Reject a check if the king escapes or the line loses the attack; do not force a mate that is not there.

forcing-reply.title: Forcing replies by the opponent
forcing-reply.observation: The opponent’s principal reply gives check after these costly decisions.
forcing-reply.goal: Choose a move accounting for the opponent’s checks.
forcing-reply.hint: Before playing, imagine the opponent’s most uncomfortable check.
forcing-reply.rule: For every candidate, first imagine the most hostile reply: check, capture, or direct threat.
forcing-reply.contrast: Only after surviving that reply should you compare slower plans.

closed-center.title: Decisions in blocked centers
closed-center.observation: Several costly decisions occurred with at least two locked pawn pairs. No strategic cause was identified.
closed-center.goal: Improve your pieces or prepare a pawn break without weakening the position.
closed-center.hint: Look for lines you can open and a piece that needs improvement. Check threats before preparing your plan.
closed-center.rule: With a locked center, identify your pawn break and improve the pieces that must support it before attacking.
closed-center.contrast: If the opponent can open the center first or has an immediate threat, address it before preparing your break.

endgame-decisions.title: Decisions with few pieces
endgame-decisions.observation: Several costly decisions occurred in low-material positions. The technical cause is not yet identified.
endgame-decisions.goal: Look for a continuation that preserves your endgame options.
endgame-decisions.hint: Compare king activity, passed pawns and immediate threats before moving.
endgame-decisions.rule: In endgames, compare king activity, passed pawns, and immediate threats before calculating exchanges.
endgame-decisions.contrast: A favorable material trade can be poor if it leaves your king passive or creates an opposing passed pawn.

path.holdoutTitle: Find the decision without knowing the theme
path.holdoutGoal: This is another position from your games. There is no hint or label: decide what the position requires.
path.holdoutPrompt: Your turn. Think as you would in a real game and play without help.
path.holdoutRecorded: Result recorded as an independent check.
path.holdoutAssisted: This counts as practice, but not as an independent check.
